title: Offshore external marine corrosion evidence
revisionReason: Revolver magazine located OUTSIDE launcher: no process-gas or internal H2S exposure assumed. Replace all former wet H2S scenarios.

environment.operatingSetting: Exposed or partially sheltered offshore platform marine atmosphere; intermittent saline spray, condensation and wet/dry cycles
environment.studyComparator: Chloride/wetting bench tests, mostly 3.5% NaCl, NOT a uniform five-alloy same-method field test
environment.actualIsoCategory: Unknown until site's corrosivity conditions or first-year standard specimen losses are evaluated

standard.scope: Classification of atmospheric corrosivity based on standard specimen first-year loss and exposure conditions; sulfur dioxide, airborne salinity, humidity/time of wetness and temperature
standard.rangesDescription: Indicative ISO 9223 category bounds for first-year standard carbon-steel specimen thickness loss only. These intervals do NOT measure our specific 1020 drum, nor permit extrapolation to aluminum, stainless steel, lifetime or local pitting.
standard.categoryDisclaimer: C5/CX selected for DESIGN REVIEW scenarios only. The user's exact offshore atmospheric classification is NOT measured or confirmed.

coatings.scope: High-durability protective paint systems and performance tests for carbon steel offshore and related structures, including CX atmosphere; NOT a standard certifying stainless/aluminum specimens or an uncoated machine assembly.
coatings.limitations: Specific coating specifications, surface preparation, tests and details require design and vendor evaluation.

6061_T6.label: Al 6061-T6
6061_T6.method: Converted from published i_corr by ASTM G102-type Faraday relation; not a directly measured penetration rate
6061_T6.test: 3.5 wt% NaCl solution; uncoated control in Table 3; no added H₂S
6061_T6.temperature: Study-specific; verify before specifying exact temperature
6061_T6.source: Effect of Citric Acid Hard Anodizing on the Mechanical Properties and Corrosion Resistance of Different Aluminum Alloys, Materials (2024), Table 3
6061_T6.warning: Uniform-equivalent conversion assumes dominant Al→Al³⁺ dissolution and ρ≈2.70 g/cm³. The source reports positive polarization hysteresis (pitting susceptibility). Rate is not verified for atmospheric exposure.
6061_T6.coastalRisk: Localized pitting; avoid dissimilar-metal contact; assess welds/coatings and crevices.

7075_T6.label: Al 7075-T6
7075_T6.method: Converted from published i_corr using same Al³⁺ model and ρ≈2.81 g/cm³; not direct penetration
7075_T6.test: 3.5 wt% NaCl solution; uncoated control in same Table 3 as 6061-T6; no added H₂S
7075_T6.temperature: Study-specific; verify before specifying exact temperature
7075_T6.source: Effect of Citric Acid Hard Anodizing on the Mechanical Properties and Corrosion Resistance of Different Aluminum Alloys, Materials (2024), Table 3
7075_T6.warning: Low i_corr in this test is not proof of 7075-T6 marine durability; susceptibility to pitting/exfoliation and galvanic corrosion is not represented by uniform-equivalent loss.
7075_T6.coastalRisk: Localized pitting, intergranular/exfoliation susceptibility and galvanic coupling.

1020_NORMALIZED.label: AISI 1020 (normalized candidate)
1020_NORMALIZED.testedGrade: SAE/AISI 1020; normalized heat treatment NOT verified
1020_NORMALIZED.reported: 0.121 mm/year by weight loss (336 h); 0.15 mm/year by polarization
1020_NORMALIZED.method: Direct reported weight-loss average (selected instead of electrochemical estimate)
1020_NORMALIZED.test: 3.5% aqueous NaCl; 336 h immersion; no intentional H₂S
1020_NORMALIZED.temperature: Not specified by accessible abstract; do not present as confirmed 25°C
1020_NORMALIZED.source: Corrosion of 1020 carbon steel in 3.5% NaCl: Analysis by mass loss and electrochemical polarization, 79th ABM Annual Congress (2026)
1020_NORMALIZED.warning: Fully immersed 336 h coupon, not outdoor marine atmosphere. Exact normalized heat treatment unknown. Corrosion rates depend on wetness, oxygen and coating state.
1020_NORMALIZED.coastalRisk: Uniform rusting and under-deposit corrosion; carbon-steel coating plan critical.

AISI_304.label: AISI 304
AISI_304.method: Published electrochemical corrosion-rate estimate after intermittent saline exposure
AISI_304.test: Intermittent 3.5 wt% NaCl exposure over 168 h; electrochemical test at 27°C; no added H₂S
AISI_304.source: Anticorrosion Behaviour of SS304 Microgroove Surfaces in Saline Water, Metals (2021), Figure 7 (flat surface after intermittent exposure)
AISI_304.warning: Flat SS304 rate in a specific saline-wetting experiment, not service-life measurement. Intermittent wetting and passive-film/crevice effects vary in real equipment.
AISI_304.coastalRisk: Chloride pitting and crevice attack near interfaces and retained salt deposits.

AISI_316.label: AISI 316 (316L research proxy)
AISI_316.method: Published electrochemical corrosion-rate v_corr, Table 5, 316L row at 298 K without Na₂S additions
AISI_316.test: Natural seawater, 298 K (25°C), no added sulfide in control; note paper also studies added sulfide in separate test groups
AISI_316.source: Corrosion Behavior of Stainless Steel in Seawater in the Presence of Sulfide, Applied Sciences (2023), Table 5 — 298 K baseline seawater, NO Na₂S
AISI_316.warning: 316L is not exact 316. Use ONLY the zero-added-sulfide 298 K control; the paper's other sulfide-dosed groups are excluded. Passive stainless alloy still susceptible to chloride pits and crevices.
AISI_316.coastalRisk: Watch crevices/fasteners and salt retention; material grade and surface state matter.

benchmark.name: Published chloride / seawater benchmarks
benchmark.computed: Uniform-rate constant-time illustrative specimen-to-CAD transfer. The model does not remove metal or account for passive film changes.
benchmark.scope: Numbers compare study-reported/converted rates across different experiments, not actual offshore rates; 7/30/90/365 day visualized values are NOT validated forecasts.

exposure.name: Marine wetting attention map
exposure.computed: Qualitative geometry-informed index 0..100 combining baseline marine salt deposition, surface-facing orientation and lower-chamber elevation proxy.
exposure.formula: index = 25 + 45*max(0,normal_world_z) + 30*(1 − clamp((world_centroid_z − z_min)/(z_max−z_min),0,1)) on selected chamber; other bodies use 25+45*max(0,normal_world_z)+15*lowElevation. Values depend on CAD orientation; intended only to prioritize visual inspection, not prediction.
exposure.notes: No CFD, wetting contact angle, salt deposition rate, condensation model, electrochemical pit kinetics or measured pit rates. Drum rotation could reverse actual pooling locations; risk positions are orientation-dependent hypotheses. No multiplying measured coupon rates by this index.
